svg.title: LogME: what the evidence integral does
svg.desc: Three panels over the weight w. Left: the Gaussian prior, centred at 0. Middle: the likelihood of y as a function of w, a Gaussian peaked at the best-fit weight 1 with height 0.159. Right: their product, peaked at the posterior mean 2/3; the area under it is the evidence 0.066, which is e to the minus 2.72.
svg.text: LogME: the evidence integral adds up prior × fit over every possible weight w (toy case: D = 1, α = β = 1, F = y = (1, −1))
Likelihood p(y | w), as a function of w
peaks at the best fit w = 1
Maximum likelihood takes the peak of the middle curve. The evidence takes the area under the right curve: every weight votes,
in proportion to how plausible it is a priori (left) and how well it explains y (middle). Each panel has its own vertical scale.
